title: HB689 (2025 Regular Session): Creates provisions relating to a prohibition on ammunition registries

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official house.mo.gov or senate.mo.gov PDF of the version named in note (via LegiScan getBillText)

operative_text:
Section 571.505 (RSMo): 3. No government entity or private person or entity shall establish, create, maintain, or facilitate a registry of ammunition sellers or purchasers within this state.
Section 571.505 (RSMo): 4. (1) No government entity shall require any person or business engaged in the sale or transfer of ammunition to collect or maintain personal information, including, but not limited to, the name, address, or identification of any purchaser, for the purpose of creating a registry. (2) No person or business shall be required to report ammunition sales or purchases to any government entity for the purpose of creating or maintaining a registry.
Section 571.505 (RSMo): 5. Any records or databases existing before the effective date of this section that contain information regarding ammunition sales or purchases shall be destroyed within ninety days of the effective date of this section. It shall be unlawful for any government entity or private person to use or disclose such records or databases to any third party after the ninety-day period.
Section 571.505 (RSMo): 8. Any person, business, or government entity that knowingly violates the provisions of this section shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than five thousand dollars per violation.
Section 571.505 (RSMo): 9. Any government official or employee who knowingly creates, maintains, or facilitates a registry in violation of this section shall be guilty of a class A misdemeanor.
